I've been farming this land for 25 years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil — it's heavy clay-loam, holds moisture okay but can get waterlogged if I over-irrigate. The well is reliable. My wife's brother works in the city now, so during busy seasons I sometimes hire day labor for harvesting, but I try to keep costs down.

**My thinking:**

For wheat, I'll use the improved variety — Jimai 22 has done well for me the past few years. Better than traditional seed, and I know the input dealers in town carry it. I'll do rotary tillage after I harvest the maize in September to break up the stubble and loosen the soil before planting in October. Three irrigations: one at sowing to ensure germination, one at jointing, one at heading. That's what my neighbors do and what's worked for me. Fertilizer — I'll put down compound fertilizer at seeding and top-dress urea at jointing. Two pesticide passes: one herbicide early, one for aphids before heading.

For maize, I go straight to hybrid seed — Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958, whatever the supply station has. After wheat harvest in June I do no-till direct seeding to save time and keep the soil from drying out too fast. It's been humid enough in July and August most years that I only need one irrigation, maybe two if it's a dry summer. One herbicide pass early, one for corn borer if I see damage.

decision.reasoning_summary: I farm all 5 mu in a wheat-maize double-crop rotation, which is standard here in Quzhou. For winter wheat I use improved seed and rotary till after maize harvest, applying compound fertilizer at seeding and urea at jointing, with three well irrigations at key growth stages and two pesticide passes for weeds and aphids, targeting around 450 kg/mu. For summer maize I switch to hybrid seed and no-till direct seeding right after wheat harvest to save time and moisture, rely mostly on summer rain with one irrigation as backup, and aim for 550 kg/mu — this system lets my household cover grain needs and sell the surplus while family members keep their off-farm income.
